1	# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-19
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-19
14	
15	- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. How should the side menu order and page through sessions once an account has more than one page's worth? → A: The list is ordered by most recent activity (`lastUserMessageAt`, descending; a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed, since sessions are only created together with their first message), and the side menu fetches further pages via `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the "CONVERSAS" section (the same infinite-scroll pattern already established for RF07's own list) — so no conversation ever becomes unreachable as the account accumulates sessions beyond a single page. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)
22	
23	A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
32	2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
33	3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)
38	
39	While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a message and observing the UI progress through the "processing/streaming" state into either "complete response" or "error," and separately by forcing a connection drop mid-response and confirming the partial text stays visible with a failure indication instead of disappearing.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** the user has just sent a message, **When** the agent begins producing a reply, **Then** the response is revealed progressively (streaming) with a visible in-progress indicator, distinct from a finished message.
48	2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
49	3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A response fails or is cut short. The user taps the failed message and gets a fresh attempt at an answer to the same question, without having to retype it, without creating a duplicate question in the history, and without disturbing the rest of the conversation.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: A direct extension of Story 2's failure state — the failure indication is only useful if there's a documented way out of it, and the requirement calls this out explicitly ("a way to try again" is part of RF04's own scope).
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a response failure, tapping the failed message to retry, and confirming a new response is generated for the same original question, with the user's question appearing exactly once in the history.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** a message shows the "Falha ao gerar resposta" state, **When** the user taps it, **Then** a new response attempt starts for that same original question, going through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as a normal response.
64	2. **Given** a retry is in progress or has completed, **When** the history is inspected, **Then** the user's original question appears exactly once — retrying never duplicates the question, only replaces the failed answer with a new attempt.
65	3. **Given** the retry itself fails again, **When** that happens, **Then** the message returns to the same failure state with the same way to try again — retrying is not limited to a single attempt.
66	
67	---
68	
69	### User Story 4 - Organizing conversations from the side menu (Priority: P2)
70	
71	A user wants to start a brand-new conversation without losing an existing one, and wants to see and return to past conversations by name and recency from the side menu.
72	
73	**Why this priority**: RF04's own scope explicitly includes the side menu's session list and "Novo Chat" action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4) — without it, a user has no way to manage more than one conversation at a time.
74	
75	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by having at least one existing conversation, opening the side menu, confirming it lists past sessions with a title and timestamp, tapping "Novo Chat," confirming the chat screen shows an empty conversation, and confirming the prior conversation is unchanged when reopened from the list.
76	
77	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
78	
79	1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.
80	2. **Given** the side menu is open, **When** the user taps the new-conversation action ("Novo Chat"), **Then** the chat screen shows an empty conversation, ready to accept a first message, without discarding any previous conversation.
81	3. **Given** the user selects a past conversation from the list, **When** it opens, **Then** its full message history is shown exactly as it was left.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)
86	
87	A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.
88	
89	**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.
90	
91	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.
92	
93	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
94	
95	1. **Given** a conversation is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the existing message history remains visible and scrollable, and a banner explains that new messages are blocked.
96	2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
97	3. **Given** the connection returns, **When** the user resumes using the screen, **Then** the send control re-enables and new messages can be sent normally.
98	4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Edge Cases
103	
104	- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.
105	- A message at or near the backend's maximum length is sent: the system either prevents exceeding that maximum before sending or surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly, without losing the text the user typed.
106	- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
107	- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.
108	- The user navigates away from a conversation (e.g., via the side menu) while a response is still streaming: when the user returns to that conversation, the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed) rather than being stuck in a stale in-progress state tied to a connection that no longer exists.
109	- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
110	- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.

112	- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
113	- Opening the side menu's conversation list, the export job, dashboard, filters, action-plan board, and every other screen or action not named in this feature's scope: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
114	
115	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
116	
117	### Functional Requirements
118	
119	- **FR-001**: The system MUST let an authenticated user send a text message in an active conversation (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`) and receive a response generated with the help of the user's own previously captured entries — the response MUST be able to reflect information from a prior entry that the user's message does not itself restate.
120	- **FR-002**: Every message the user sends and every response the agent produces MUST be persisted as part of the conversation (`chat_messages`) and MUST still be present, in the same order, the next time that conversation is opened — including after the app is closed and reopened (`GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages`).
121	- **FR-003**: Sending a chat message MUST NOT create a journal entry under any circumstance handled by this unit; the only path from a chat message to a persisted entry is the explicit save action of a later unit (RF10), which this unit does not implement.
122	- **FR-004**: While a response is being generated, the system MUST render it in a visibly distinct "processing/streaming" state (content revealed progressively, in-progress indicator) and MUST transition it to one of exactly two end states: "complete response" (final text, timestamp shown, no in-progress indicator) or an error state ("Falha ao gerar resposta," shown in place of the timestamp). 123	- **FR-005**: If the response stream is interrupted before completion (connection drop, backend error, or any other cause), the system MUST keep whatever partial text had already arrived visible, together with the failure indication — it MUST NOT remove, hide, or blank out a partial message.
124	- **FR-006**: A message in the error state MUST be tappable to trigger a retry (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`) that regenerates the response to that same original question. A retry MUST NOT duplicate the user's original question in the conversation, and MUST go through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as any other response. Retrying MUST remain available after a retry itself fails, with no fixed limit on the number of attempts, and MUST remain available on any message in the error state regardless of how much later conversation exists after it.
125	- **FR-007**: While a response in the current conversation is streaming or sitting in the error state awaiting retry, the system MUST keep the message-send control disabled, re-enabling it only once that response reaches a final state (complete, or retried to a new resolution) — so a single conversation never has two responses in flight at once.
126	- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp, ordered by most recent activity (latest `lastUserMessageAt` first). If the account has more sessions than fit in one backend page, the list MUST fetch further pages via the endpoint's `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the section, so every conversation stays reachable.
127	- **FR-009**: The side menu MUST offer a "Novo Chat" action that opens the chat screen in an empty conversation state, ready to accept a first message, without discarding or altering any existing conversation. Selecting an existing conversation from the list MUST open it with its full message history intact, exactly as it was left.
128	- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. 129	- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.
130	- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
131	- **FR-013**: The screen MUST reuse the existing session-expiration handling (RF03/RF07's "Sessão expirada" overlay: history and scroll position preserved, re-authentication returning to the same conversation state) rather than introducing a separate expiration treatment for chat.
132	- **FR-014**: This unit MUST NOT implement the "save message as entry" button (RF10), the proactive-insight card (RF08), AI-persona selection as an active setting (extension, requirements section 2 — persona is only read at session creation as whatever the backend already returns), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
133	
134	### Key Entities
135	
136	- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
137	- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). 138	- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. It is retrieved automatically for every response and is not displayed to the user as a separate citation list — the prototype defines no such element — but it is what makes a response "grounded" rather than generic, per User Story 1.
139	
140	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
141	
142	### Measurable Outcomes
143	
144	- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
145	- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.
146	- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced stream-interruption scenarios, the partial response text remains visible on screen together with its failure indication — never disappearing.
147	- **SC-004**: Across repeated retries of the same failed message, the user's original question appears exactly once in the conversation history, with zero observed duplicates.
148	- **SC-005**: Conversation history is preserved exactly (same messages, same order) across an app restart and across switching away from and back to a conversation via the side menu, in 100% of tested cases.
149	- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.

151	
152	## Assumptions
153	
154	- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. 156	- A session's `personaSnapshot` (requirements section 2's persona extension) is read and stored as whatever the backend returns at session creation; this unit does not add any UI for choosing or changing it.

**Created**: 2026-10-19

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-19

- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. How should the side menu order and page through sessions once an account has more than one page's worth? → A: The list is ordered by most recent activity (`lastUserMessageAt`, descending; a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed, since sessions are only created together with their first message), and the side menu fetches further pages via `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the "CONVERSAS" section (the same infinite-scroll pattern already established for RF07's own list) — so no conversation ever becomes unreachable as the account accumulates sessions beyond a single page. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)

A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).

---

### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)

While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.

**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.

2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.

---

### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)

1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.

3. **Given** the user selects a past conversation from the list, **When** it opens, **Then** its full message history is shown exactly as it was left.

- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). A failed message is the one eligible for retry; retrying produces a new resolution for the same original question rather than a new message pair.
- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. It is retrieved automatically for every response and is not displayed to the user as a separate citation list — the prototype defines no such element — but it is what makes a response "grounded" rather than generic, per User Story 1.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.
- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced stream-interruption scenarios, the partial response text remains visible on screen together with its failure indication — never disappearing.
- **SC-004**: Across repeated retries of the same failed message, the user's original question appears exactly once in the conversation history, with zero observed duplicates.
- **SC-005**: Conversation history is preserved exactly (same messages, same order) across an app restart and across switching away from and back to a conversation via the side menu, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
- **SC-007**: On an account with more conversations than one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` returns, 100% of them remain reachable from the side menu by scrolling, with zero conversations permanently hidden.

## Assumptions

- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
- The "context" step of the backend's streaming sequence (`message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`) is an internal signal the client may use to drive its own progress indicator, not a citation list rendered to the user — the prototype defines no UI for displaying which entries were used.
- A session's `personaSnapshot` (requirements section 2's persona extension) is read and stored as whatever the backend returns at session creation; this unit does not add any UI for choosing or changing it.
- Network-error handling for this screen's write calls (send, retry, create session) follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09) — no new error-presentation style is introduced specifically for chat.
- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.
- The composer's existing disabled-by-default rendering (already scaffolded by F000) becomes conditionally enabled by this unit whenever there is non-empty text to send and no response currently in flight or awaiting retry for that conversation — it does not require a separate redesign of the composer itself.

is the unit that makes Home/Chat's currently-inert, fully-disabled composer (F000's own scaffold,
`home_chat_shell_page.dart`) and the side menu's currently-static `AppDrawer` actually work.

## Summary

Home/Chat gains a live, persisted conversation with the backend's RAG-grounded agent
(`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`, SSE: `message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`), and the side
menu's `AppDrawer` gains a paginated, offline-cached "CONVERSAS" list (`GET /chat/sessions`) plus a working
"Novo Chat" action. A new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ChatSession`/`ChatMessage`/`ChatSessionsPage`/`ChatStreamEvent`/`ChatTitleDeriver` (domain), `ChatRemoteDataSource`/
`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` (data), and two blocs — `ChatBloc` (the one live conversation: streaming,
retry, lazy session creation, composer gating) and `ChatSessionsBloc` (the side menu's own paginated list,
mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s RF07-established shape almost exactly, research.md R7). `core/network/ApiClient`
gains one new, chat-agnostic method, `sseStream()`, built on `dio`'s own `ResponseType.stream` with a
hand-rolled SSE frame parser (research.md R1) — no new package. `core/network/ConnectivityChecker` gains a
live `onConnectivityChanged` stream (research.md R8), layered on top of (not replacing) the existing
synchronous `hasConnection()` pre-check every write path in this app already uses. A new, Keychain-backed
`ChatLocalCache` (mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own pattern) persists the session list, each individually-
opened session's message history, and the last-active session id, satisfying spec.md's Clarification 3
(offline browsing covers every previously-opened conversation, not just the one open at disconnect) and its
own Assumptions (resuming the last conversation on app restart). A new chat message or its own session is
never created eagerly — only lazily, at the moment a first message is actually sent (FR-010) — and the title
sent with that creation call is derived client-side from the message's own text by a new, pure
`ChatTitleDeriver` (research.md R6), since the backend has no auto-titling or rename endpoint of its own. No
new `go_router` route is added: Home/Chat stays the one existing, unparameterized `/home` screen, swapping its
displayed conversation in place via the two blocs it's now provided with (research.md R7) — "Novo Chat" and
selecting a past conversation from the drawer are both in-place state transitions, not navigations.

(for the new `ChatLocalCache`), `connectivity_plus` (its own `onConnectivityChanged` stream, previously
unused — `ConnectivityChecker` only ever called `checkConnectivity()` once per check before this unit); dev-only
`mocktail`, `bloc_test`. SSE is consumed via a ~30-line hand-rolled parser over `dio`'s existing byte-stream
support, explicitly chosen over any third-party SSE package (research.md R1) — the OpenAPI contract's own
schema for both SSE operations is `content: text/event-stream` / `{type: string}`, i.e. genuinely no typed
shape to generate a client from.

## Complexity Tracking

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-rolled SSE parsing in `ApiClient` (research.md R1) | `chat.messages.send`/`.retry` are this app's first and only streaming endpoints; the OpenAPI contract gives them no typed response shape (`text/event-stream`/`{type: string}`) for `call()`'s existing JSON-only path to handle | A third-party SSE package — rejected: introduces a second HTTP-stack assumption alongside `dio`, for a 5-event-type protocol spoken to exactly one backend (research.md R1) |
| Two blocs (`ChatBloc` + `ChatSessionsBloc`) instead of one | The live conversation (streaming, retry, composer gating) and the side menu's paginated list are independently-failing, independently-paginated concerns — exactly the two-concerns split `RecordsBloc` staying independent of `SessionBloc`/`VaultBloc` already establishes as this codebase's norm | One combined bloc — rejected: conflates two state shapes with genuinely different failure/pagination semantics into one, as reasoned in research.md R7 |
| A new `ChatLocalCache` (3 keys) rather than reusing `EntriesLocalCache`'s shape as-is | Chat needs to cache *two* independent things (a session list and N sessions' individual message histories) plus a small scalar (`lastActiveSessionId`) — `EntriesLocalCache` only ever caches one flat list | Reusing `EntriesLocalCache` directly — rejected: it has no concept of "per-session" keying, and bolting one on would make it do two unrelated jobs for two unrelated features |

*No entry needed beyond these three — each is either this unit's first genuinely new mechanism (SSE) or a
direct, justified extension of an already-proven pattern (two blocs mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s own split; a
cache mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own rationale).*

561	  branch is built as part of that same function and cannot be split; this phase is otherwise test-only.
562	- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational and US1's `_consumeTurn` (T021), which it reuses verbatim
563	  for the retry's own stream consumption.
564	- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: depends on Foundational only — independent of US1/US2/US3's own tasks (no shared
565	  code with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery).
566	- **User Story 5 (Phase 7)**: depends on Foundational's `_loadSession`/`ChatSessionsBloc` cache-fallback logic
567	  (already built there) and on `ChatComposer` (T022, US1) for its own offline-disabling test.
568	- **Polish (Phase 8)**: depends on all five user stories being complete.
569	
570	### Within Each Phase
571	
572	- Tasks touching the *same* file (`chat_bloc.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`,
573	  `service_locator.dart`, `app_router.dart`) are listed in the sequential order they must be applied.
574	- Tasks creating a *new* file with no dependency on that phase's other new files are marked `[P]`.
575	- Test tasks are marked `[P]` relative to each other (distinct test files); each still depends on its
576	  corresponding implementation task(s) existing to pass.
577	
578	### Parallel Opportunities
579	
580	- T001, T003–T008, T013, T014, T016 (Foundational's entities/events/states/widgets/transport) can all run in
581	  parallel — ten independent files with no cross-dependencies among them.
582	- T010 and T011 (local cache, remote data source) can run in parallel with each other once T001–T008 land.
583	- All test tasks within a single user story phase can run in parallel with each other.
584	- User Story 4 (side menu) can be implemented in parallel with User Stories 1–3 (the live conversation) by a
585	  second developer, since neither `ChatSessionsBloc` nor `AppDrawer`'s "CONVERSAS" section shares any code path
586	  with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery.
587	
588	---
589	
590	## Parallel Example: Foundational Phase
591	
592	```bash
593	# Launch the independent entity/transport/widget files together:
594	Task: "Create SseFrame in lib/core/network/sse_frame.dart"
595	Task: "Add onConnectivityChanged to lib/core/network/connectivity_checker.dart"
596	Task: "Create ChatSession/ChatPersona in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart"
597	Task: "Create ChatRole/ChatMessageStatus/ChatMessage in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart"
598	Task: "Create ChatStreamEvent in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart"
599	Task: "Create ChatTitleDeriver in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart"
600	Task: "Create ChatEvent in lib/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_event.dart"
601	Task: "Create ChatMessageBubble in lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_message_bubble.dart"
602	```
603	
604	---
605	
606	## Implementation Strategy
607	
608	### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)
609	
610	1. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (transport, data layer, entities, `ChatBloc`'s conversation-loading core).
611	2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (lazy session creation, send, stream, persist, no entry created).
612	3. **STOP and VALIDATE**: seed a prior entry, send a related message, confirm the grounded response (SC-001);
613	   restart the app and confirm the exchange persists (SC-005).
614	4. Demo/ship if ready — this alone delivers RF04's "entire premise" (spec.md, User Story 1's "Why this
615	   priority").
616	
617	### Incremental Delivery
618	
619	1. Foundational → User Story 1 (MVP: grounded, persisted conversation).
620	2. + User Story 2 (the three-state visual contract — mostly tests over already-built engine behavior).
621	3. + User Story 3 (tap-to-retry on a failed response).
622	4. + User Story 4 (side menu: list, paginate, "Novo Chat") — independently buildable in parallel with 2–3.
623	5. + User Story 5 (offline banner + multi-conversation offline coverage).
624	6. + Polish (verification gates, manual walkthrough).
625	
626	Each stage adds value without breaking the previous one, matching spec.md's own stated priority order (P1, P1,
627	P2, P2, P3).

# Tasks: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) and RNF09 (Either +
15/15 error scenarios) both "PASS (gate carried into tasks)", and every file under `contracts/` carries its own
"Test scenarios this contract owns" table plus `quickstart.md`'s "Automated checks" section — this is this
feature's own design material requesting test tasks, not an invented addition.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (spec.md's five User Stories: P1, P1, P2, P2, P3). This
feature introduces one entirely new feature folder (`lib/features/chat/`, two blocs) plus two `core/network/`
extensions. Loading a conversation (resume-last / switch / new-empty) is needed by every single story — even
US4's "Novo Chat" and US5's offline browsing go through the same `_loadSession` path — so the shared
transport/data/repository layer and `ChatBloc`'s own "load a conversation" machinery are necessarily
Foundational; each User Story phase then adds that story's own handler bodies, widgets, and tests on top.

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (plan.md's "Project Type"): `lib/features/chat/{domain,data,presentation}/`, mirrored
under `test/features/chat/...`; two `core/network/` files extended in place; `lib/features/home/` extended in
place. No `backend/`/`frontend/` split, no `.env`/native project file touched, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` (Constraints, FR-014).

---

## Phase 1: Setup

No setup tasks. `plan.md`'s "Primary Dependencies" is explicit — "No additions... reuses the full existing
stack" — and the Project Structure's "Structure Decision" already fixes every new file's location. Proceed
directly to Foundational.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: the shared transport (`SseFrame`/`ApiClient.sseStream`, live connectivity), the domain entities,
the data layer (`ChatRemoteDataSource`/`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`), and `ChatBloc`'s own
"resume/switch/new empty conversation" machinery (`ChatStarted`/`ConversationSelected`/
`NewConversationRequested`/`_loadSession`) that every user story's handlers build on top of.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story phase can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T001 [P] Create `lib/core/network/sse_frame.dart`: `class SseFrame extends Equatable` with `final String
  event` and `final String data` (raw JSON text, parsed by the caller — `ApiClient` itself stays generic),
  `props => [event, data]` (data-model.md, contracts/sse-transport-extension.md).

- [ ] T002 Extend `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` with `Stream<Either<Failure, SseFrame>> sseStream(String
  function, {required String method, Map<String, dynamic>? body, List<String>? pathSegments, AuthMode authMode
  = AuthMode.userSession})` per contracts/sse-transport-extension.md: issues the request via
  `_dio.request<ResponseBody>(url, options: Options(method: ..., responseType: ResponseType.stream, headers:
  {'apikey': _anonKey, 'Authorization': 'Bearer $bearer'}))` (same header-building logic `call()` already
  uses); decodes each byte chunk as UTF-8 (`allowMalformed: true`) into a buffer and splits frames on the
  blank-line (`\n\n`) SSE delimiter, parsing `event:`/`data:` lines per frame (multiple consecutive `data:`
  lines joined with `\n`; any other SSE field ignored); yields `Right(SseFrame(...))` per parsed frame in
  arrival order; on `DioException`, yields **exactly one** `Left(_mapException(e))` — reusing the existing
  `_mapException` verbatim, no second failure-mapping implementation — as the stream's **last** item, then the
  stream closes (no further iteration of `response.data!.stream` after the exception). `call()` is unchanged.
  Depends on T001.

- [ ] T003 [P] Add `Stream<bool> get onConnectivityChanged` to `lib/core/network/connectivity_checker.dart`
  (research.md R8): wraps `Connectivity().onConnectivityChanged`'s own broadcast stream, mapping "any result
  `!= ConnectivityResult.none`" → `true` — the exact same predicate `hasConnection()` already uses. The existing
  synchronous `hasConnection()` method is unchanged (R8's own write-path pre-check still calls it directly).

- [ ] T004 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart`: `enum ChatPersona { analitico,
  empatico, socratico }`; `class ChatSession extends Equatable` with `required` fields `id` (`String`), `title`
  (`String`), `personaSnapshot` (`ChatPersona` — read-only here, FR-014, never written back), `userMessageCount`
  (`int`), `lastUserMessageAt` (`DateTime?` — "nullable per schema; in practice always non-null once listed"),
  `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (`DateTime`); `props` over all seven fields (data-model.md).

- [ ] T005 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart`: `enum ChatRole { user, assistant
  }`; `enum ChatMessageStatus { streaming, complete, failed }`; `class ChatMessage extends Equatable` with
  `required` fields `id` (`String` — `'local-<timestamp>'`-prefixed until reconciled with the server's real id,
  research.md R5), `sessionId`, `role`, `content` (grows incrementally while `status == streaming`), `seq`
  (`int`), `status`, `retryCount` (`int`), `createdAt`; `bool get isOptimistic => id.startsWith('local-')`;
  `props` over `[id, sessionId, role, content, seq, status, retryCount, createdAt]` (data-model.md).

- [ ] T006 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_sessions_page.dart`: `class ChatSessionsPage
  extends Equatable` with `final List<ChatSession> sessions` and `final String? nextCursor` (`meta.nextCursor`
  verbatim; `null` = last page) — directly mirrors `EntriesPage`'s own shape. Depends on T004.

- [ ] T007 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart`: `sealed class ChatStreamEvent
  extends Equatable`; `MessageCreated({required String userMessageId, required String assistantMessageId})`;
  `ContextReceived()` (no fields); `TokenReceived(String delta)`; `StreamDone({required String
  assistantMessageId, required String content, required DateTime createdAt})`. No `ErrorEvent` variant — both a
  business-level `error` SSE frame and a transport-level `DioException` become a `Left(Failure)` on the same
  `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>` (data-model.md, research.md R2).

- [ ] T008 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart`: `class ChatTitleDeriver`
  with a private constructor, `static const _maxLength = 48`, and `static String derive(String
  firstMessageText)` — collapses internal whitespace/newlines to single spaces via `replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'),
  ' ')`, trims, and when the result's length exceeds 48 returns `'${collapsed.substring(0, 48)}…'`, otherwise
  the collapsed string unchanged. Pure, total; never returns an empty string for non-empty input; no
  `package:flutter` import, no I/O (research.md R6, Principle V).

- [ ] T009 Create `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`: abstract `ChatRepository` with
  `Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession({required String title})`; `Future<Either<Failure,
  ChatSessionsPage>> listSessions({String? cursor, int? limit})`; `List<ChatSession> get cachedSessions`;
  `Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId)`; `List<ChatMessage>?
  cachedMessages(String sessionId)` (`null` = this session's history was never fetched while online); `Future<void>
  setLastActiveSessionId(String? sessionId)`; `Future<String?> get lastActiveSessionId`; `Stream<Either<Failure,
  ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage({required String sessionId, required String content})`;
  `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> retryMessage({required String sessionId, required String
  userMessageId})` — exactly data-model.md's interface. Depends on T004, T005, T006, T007.

- [ ] T010 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/data/chat_local_cache.dart` (research.md R4): Keychain-backed

**Goal**: send a message into a conversation (creating its session lazily on the first send, FR-010), stream a

entry (FR-001/FR-002/FR-003).

**Independent Test**: seed a prior entry on a specific topic, send a chat message that references that topic

  with the backend's own `nextCursor`), #2 (`SessionsStarted` fails outright, nothing cached →
  `ChatSessionsLoadFailure`), #4 (`SessionsRefreshRequested` fired while already `ChatSessionsLoaded`, and the
  refresh itself fails → the existing `sessions` list is untouched, never regresses), #5
  (`SessionsNextPageRequested` when `hasReachedEnd` is already `true` → no repository call), #6
  (`SessionsNextPageRequested` succeeds → `sessions` grows by exactly the new page's items, no duplicates,
  `nextCursor` updated — SC-007), #8 (two `SessionsNextPageRequested` fired back-to-back before the first
  resolves → the second is a no-op while `isLoadingMore` is already `true`). Depends on T038.

- [ ] T044 [P] [US4] Widget tests for the "CONVERSAS" section and "Novo Chat" in
  `test/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` (new file): the section lists each loaded
  session with its title + timestamp; tapping a session row dispatches `ConversationSelected(session.id)` and
  closes the drawer; tapping "Novo Chat" dispatches `NewConversationRequested`; scrolling to the bottom of the
  section dispatches `SessionsNextPageRequested`. Depends on T041.

- [ ] T045 [P] [US4] `bloc_test` case in `test/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_bloc_test.dart` — contract
  scenario #11: `NewConversationRequested` while a previous conversation has in-memory messages leaves that
  previous conversation's own `ChatLocalCache` entry untouched — only `lastActiveSessionId` changes; selecting
  it again later still shows its full history (already-built Foundational behavior, T012/T015; this task is
  test-only). Depends on T012, T015.

**Checkpoint**: Stories 1–4 — the side menu organizes and paginates conversations; "Novo Chat" never discards
an existing one.

---

## Phase 7: User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)

**Goal**: every previously-opened conversation's history and the side menu's own list stay visible, scrollable,
and switchable offline; the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner; sending resumes automatically
on reconnect (FR-011/FR-012).

**Independent Test**: load a conversation, go offline, confirm history stays visible/scrollable and the
composer is disabled with a banner; switch to a different previously-opened conversation offline and confirm
its own cached history shows correctly; select a never-opened conversation offline and confirm the
no-connection state instead of any content; reconnect and confirm the composer re-enables automatically.

> The offline cache-fallback logic itself (`_loadSession`'s cached/no-cache branching, `ChatSessionsBloc`'s own
> `cachedSessions` fallback) is already built in Foundational (T015, T038) as a direct consequence of
> Clarification 3's scope. This phase's own new work is the offline banner widget and its wiring, plus the
> scenario-specific tests proving multi-conversation offline coverage.

### Implementation for User Story 5

- [ ] T046 [P] [US5] Create `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_offline_banner.dart`: "Sem conexão —
  histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas" (prototype-extract.md §2.2), `DesignTokens.colorInfoOffline`
  background per data-model.md's token-reuse table.

- [ ] T047 [US5] Render `ChatOfflineBanner` in `lib/features/home/presentation/pages/home_chat_shell_page.dart`
  whenever `ChatReady.isOffline` is `true` (FR-011). Depends on T019, T046.

### Tests for User Story 5

- [ ] T048 [P] [US5] Offline cache-fallback tests across multiple previously-opened conversations —
  chat-repository.md contract scenario #4 (`cachedMessages('never-opened')` returns `null`) in
  `test/features/chat/data/chat_repository_impl_test.dart`; chat-bloc.md contract scenarios #3 (`ChatStarted`/
  `_loadSession` with a failed fetch and nothing cached → `loadFailure` set) and #4 (a failed fetch but a cache
  exists → the cached messages are shown, no `loadFailure`) in
  `test/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_bloc_test.dart` — together proving SC-006/Clarification 3. Depends
  on T012, T015.

- [ ] T049 [P] [US5] `bloc_test` case for `ChatSessionsBloc`'s own offline fallback in
  `test/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_sessions_bloc_test.dart` — contract scenario #3: `SessionsStarted`
  fails but `cachedSessions` is non-empty → `ChatSessionsLoaded(sessions: <cached>, nextCursor: null)`,
  satisfying FR-011's "the side menu's own CONVERSAS list" staying browsable offline. Depends on T038.

- [ ] T050 [P] [US5] Widget test confirming `ChatComposer`'s disabled rendering while `ChatReady.isOffline` is
  `true`, and that it re-enables automatically (no manual action) once `isOffline` flips back to `false` —
  "within one interaction of connectivity returning" (SC-006) — in
  `test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_composer_test.dart`. Depends on T022.

**Checkpoint**: All five user stories are independently functional — the full RF04 scope works end-to-end.

---

## Phase 8: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Purpose**: the project's own verification gates (RNF06/RNF07, quickstart.md).

- [ ] T051 Run `fvm flutter analyze` and `dart test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` plus `dart
  test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart`, confirming both continue to pass unmodified against the new
  `lib/features/chat/` folder — `chat/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart`, and `ChatBloc`/
  `ChatSessionsBloc` neither import each other nor `SessionBloc` (manually re-confirmed, since the architecture
  test only mechanically enforces cross-*feature* imports — quickstart.md "Automated checks"). Depends on all
  prior tasks.

- [ ] T052 Run `fvm flutter test --coverage`, then `lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o
  coverage/domain.info` and `genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html`; confirm ≥80% domain
  coverage (RNF07 gate) including `chat_title_deriver.dart`, `ChatMessage`'s status-transition shape, and
  `ChatStreamEvent`'s sealed variants. Depends on T051.

- [ ] T053 Execute quickstart.md's manual verification walkthrough on a device/Simulator — Stories 1–5 plus
  "Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once" (empty/whitespace message, the 8000-character cap,
  double-send-while-awaiting, session-expiry mid-stream, navigate-away-mid-stream, zero-conversations
  first-ever use) — using a seeded prior entry
  (`docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`) and an account with more sessions than one
  `chat-sessions-list` page. Depends on T052.

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: no dependencies — can start immediately. **BLOCKS** every user story phase (every
  story needs `ChatBloc`'s "load a conversation" machinery at minimum).
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: depends on Foundational only. MVP.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: depends on Foundational **and** US1's `_consumeTurn` (T021) — its failure-handling
  branch is built as part of that same function and cannot be split; this phase is otherwise test-only.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational and US1's `_consumeTurn` (T021), which it reuses verbatim
  for the retry's own stream consumption.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: depends on Foundational only — independent of US1/US2/US3's own tasks (no shared
  code with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery).
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7)**: depends on Foundational's `_loadSession`/`ChatSessionsBloc` cache-fallback logic
  (already built there) and on `ChatComposer` (T022, US1) for its own offline-disabling test.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each Phase

- Tasks touching the *same* file (`chat_bloc.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`,
  `service_locator.dart`, `app_router.dart`) are listed in the sequential order they must be applied.
- Tasks creating a *new* file with no dependency on that phase's other new files are marked `[P]`.
- Test tasks are marked `[P]` relative to each other (distinct test files); each still depends on its
  corresponding implementation task(s) existing to pass.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T001, T003–T008, T013, T014, T016 (Foundational's entities/events/states/widgets/transport) can all run in
  parallel — ten independent files with no cross-dependencies among them.
- T010 and T011 (local cache, remote data source) can run in parallel with each other once T001–T008 land.
- All test tasks within a single user story phase can run in parallel with each other.
- User Story 4 (side menu) can be implemented in parallel with User Stories 1–3 (the live conversation) by a
  second developer, since neither `ChatSessionsBloc` nor `AppDrawer`'s "CONVERSAS" section shares any code path
  with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery.

---

## Parallel Example: Foundational Phase

```bash
# Launch the independent entity/transport/widget files together:
Task: "Create SseFrame in lib/core/network/sse_frame.dart"
Task: "Add onConnectivityChanged to lib/core/network/connectivity_checker.dart"
Task: "Create ChatSession/ChatPersona in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart"
Task: "Create ChatRole/ChatMessageStatus/ChatMessage in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart"
Task: "Create ChatStreamEvent in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart"
Task: "Create ChatTitleDeriver in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart"
Task: "Create ChatEvent in lib/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_event.dart"
Task: "Create ChatMessageBubble in lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_message_bubble.dart"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (transport, data layer, entities, `ChatBloc`'s conversation-loading core).
2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (lazy session creation, send, stream, persist, no entry created).
3. **STOP and VALIDATE**: seed a prior entry, send a related message, confirm the grounded response (SC-001);
   restart the app and confirm the exchange persists (SC-005).
4. Demo/ship if ready — this alone delivers RF04's "entire premise" (spec.md, User Story 1's "Why this
   priority").

### Incremental Delivery

1. Foundational → User Story 1 (MVP: grounded, persisted conversation).
2. + User Story 2 (the three-state visual contract — mostly tests over already-built engine behavior).
3. + User Story 3 (tap-to-retry on a failed response).
4. + User Story 4 (side menu: list, paginate, "Novo Chat") — independently buildable in parallel with 2–3.
5. + User Story 5 (offline banner + multi-conversation offline coverage).
6. + Polish (verification gates, manual walkthrough).

Each stage adds value without breaking the previous one, matching spec.md's own stated priority order (P1, P1,
P2, P2, P3).

## Specification Analysis Report

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|----|----------|----------|--------------|---------|----------------|
| C1 | Coverage Gap | CRITICAL | contracts/sse-transport-extension.md:90-98; plan.md:131 (RNF09 row); plan.md:62-69 (Testing) | `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF09 "PASS (gate carried into tasks)" and claims the 3 required failure scenarios "are each exercised at the transport layer (`contracts/sse-transport-extension.md`'s own scenario table)." That table defines 5 concrete test scenarios for `ApiClient.sseStream()`/`SseFrame` parsing (chunk-split frames, timeout mid-stream, no-response offline, bare `context` frame, multi-line `data:`). `tasks.md` has no task creating `test/core/network/api_client_sse_test.dart` (or any file) that exercises any of these 5 scenarios — T001/T002 only implement `sseStream`, with no paired test task. | Add a Foundational-phase test task (e.g. after T002) creating `test/core/network/api_client_sse_test.dart` that covers sse-transport-extension.md's 5 scenarios, so the RNF09 gate claim is actually backed by a task. |
| I1 | Inconsistency / Correctness | HIGH | contracts/chat-bloc.md:24, 142-170, 181-203; spec.md:108 (Edge Cases) | `_turnGeneration` (research.md R9's "defensive" guard inside `_consumeTurn`) is only incremented in `_onMessageSubmitted`/`_onMessageRetryRequested`. It is **not** incremented by `_onConversationSelected`/`_onNewConversationRequested`/`ChatStarted`. spec.md's own Edge Cases section requires: "The user navigates away from a conversation... while a response is still streaming: when the user returns... the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded... rather than being stuck in a stale state tied to a connection that no longer exists." Because switching conversations doesn't bump the generation counter, an in-flight `emit.forEach` turn from conversation A can still pass the `generation != _turnGeneration` check and apply `_appendToken`/`_completeMessage`/`_applyFailure` mutations against whatever `ChatReady` state is current — which, after the switch, belongs to conversation B — with no contract scenario or task defining/testing this interaction. | Bump `_turnGeneration` (or an equivalent "active session" guard) on `_onConversationSelected`/`_onNewConversationRequested` too, so a turn from the conversation navigated away from stops updating `state` once the conversation has changed. Add a bloc_test scenario covering this. |
| C2 | Coverage Gap | MEDIUM | contracts/chat-bloc.md:214-229 (#2, #6, #12); contracts/chat-repository.md:225-236 (#3); contracts/chat-sessions-bloc.md:105-116 (#7) | Several contract-documented test scenarios have no task mapping anywhere in `tasks.md`, unlike every other scenario in these same tables (each of which is explicitly cited by task number): chat-bloc.md #2 (`ChatStarted` success w/ stored id), #6 (`MessageSubmitted` while offline, ties to FR-012), #12 (`_ConnectivityChanged` mid-turn); chat-repository.md #3 (`listMessages` success populates `cachedMessages`); chat-sessions-bloc.md #7 (`AuthExpiredFailure` on a next-page fetch). | Fold these into the existing nearest test tasks (T027, T026, T043) by name, the same way every other scenario in these tables is already explicitly cited. |
| U1 | Underspecification | MEDIUM | spec.md:16 (Clarification 2); data-model.md:104; contracts/chat-repository.md (listSessions) | Clarification 2 itself states `GET /chat/sessions` "carries no documented sort order" in the OpenAPI contract (confirmed: `chat.sessions.list`'s response schema has no ordering semantics). FR-008/data-model.md nonetheless assume the backend already returns sessions ordered by `lastUserMessageAt` descending ("backend-ordered — see contracts/chat-repository.md"), and `ChatSessionsBloc`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` never sort or verify this client-side. No task validates this assumption or adds a defensive sort. | Either add a client-side stable sort by `lastUserMessageAt` desc within a page in `ChatRepositoryImpl.listSessions` (safe since it only reorders within one already-fetched page), or add a manual quickstart.md check confirming the account's own data is already backend-ordered as assumed. |
| L1 | Inconsistency (cosmetic) | LOW | data-model.md:221-247; contracts/sse-transport-extension.md:14-15; tasks.md T002 | `data-model.md` documents `sseStream` as a plain method added to `class ApiClient`; `contracts/sse-transport-extension.md` implements it as `extension on ApiClient { ... }`. Both access `ApiClient`'s private fields (`_dio`, `_anonKey`, `_mapException`), which in Dart requires the extension to live in the same library file as `ApiClient` (i.e., inside `api_client.dart` itself, matching T002's framing) rather than in the separate `sse_frame.dart` file the Source Code tree lists. Not a blocking contradiction, but worth resolving before implementation to avoid an accidental private-member-access compile error if `sseStream` is placed in `sse_frame.dart`. | Clarify in `plan.md`/`data-model.md` that the extension (if used) must be declared inside `api_client.dart`, with `sse_frame.dart` holding only the `SseFrame` class. |

## Coverage Summary Table

| Requirement Key | Has Task? | Task IDs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | ✅ | T020, T021, T025–T027 | |
| FR-002 | ✅ | T011, T012, T015 | chat-repository.md #3 persistence scenario itself ungapped — see C2 |

| FR-013 | ✅ (partial) | T015, T019 | reauth-forwarding wired; no dedicated bloc_test scenario for mid-stream `AuthExpiredFailure` → `reauthRequired` |
| FR-014 | ✅ | T051 | |

| SC-005 | ✅ | T045, Foundational cache tasks | |
| SC-006 | ✅ | T048–T050 | |
| SC-007 | ✅ | T043 | |

## Constitution Alignment Issues

- **CRITICAL** — RNF09 ("every write endpoint... each covered by `mocktail` tests") is marked PASS in `plan.md` with an explicit pointer to `contracts/sse-transport-extension.md`'s scenario table as the proof, but no task in `tasks.md` implements those tests (see C1). This is a gate claimed satisfied that is not actually scheduled.

## Unmapped Tasks

None found — every task in `tasks.md` traces to a Foundational dependency, a User Story's FR(s), or a Polish/verification gate (RNF06/07, quickstart.md).

## Metrics

- Total Functional Requirements: 14 (all 14 have ≥1 task — 100% FR-level coverage)
- Total Success Criteria (buildable): 7 (all 7 have ≥1 task)
- Total Tasks: 53
- Ambiguity Count: 0 significant (vague terms like "clear failure indication" are all backed by concrete, named UI states)
- Duplication Count: 0
- Critical Issues Count: 1 (C1)
- High Issues Count: 1 (I1)
- Medium Issues Count: 2 (C2, U1)
- Low Issues Count: 1 (L1)

## Next Actions

- **Resolve C1 before `/speckit-implement`**: add the missing `ApiClient.sseStream()` test task — it backs a CRITICAL/constitution-gated (RNF09) claim that is currently unfulfilled.
- **Strongly recommend resolving I1 before implementing Foundational (T015)**: the generation-guard gap is a real correctness risk for an Edge Case spec.md explicitly calls out, and T015 is where the fix belongs.
- C2, U1, L1 are MEDIUM/LOW — safe to proceed, but cheap to fix by editing `tasks.md` directly (fold missing scenario citations into T026/T027/T043) and `chat_repository_impl.dart`'s planned `listSessions` (U1).
- Suggested commands: "Manually edit tasks.md to add a transport-layer test task for sse-transport-extension.md's 5 scenarios" (C1); "Manually edit chat-bloc.md's contract + tasks.md T015 to bump `_turnGeneration` on conversation switch" (I1).

## Offer Remediation

Would you like me to suggest concrete remediation edits (to `tasks.md` and/or the `contracts/chat-bloc.md` contract) for C1 and I1, the two highest-priority issues?

Here are concrete remediation edits for the two priority findings. I'm presenting them as proposed diffs — not applying them, per the read-only constraint of this analysis.

## Remediation for C1 (CRITICAL — missing SSE transport tests)

**New task**, inserted into `tasks.md`'s Phase 2 (Foundational), directly after T002, with everything after it renumbered by one (T003→T004, …, T053→T054):

```markdown
- [ ] T003 [P] Create `test/core/network/api_client_sse_test.dart` per contracts/sse-transport-extension.md's
  "Test scenarios this contract owns" table: scenario #1 (3 frames split across 2 byte chunks mid-frame — all 3
  parsed correctly, no dropped/duplicated bytes across the boundary); #2 (a `DioException` with
  `type: connectionTimeout` thrown after 1 frame already yielded — exactly `Right(frame1)` then
  `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` as the stream's last item); #3 (a `DioException` with no `response` at all —
  `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` as the final item); #4 (`event: context\ndata: {}` — yielded as an ordinary
  `Right(SseFrame(event: 'context', data: '{}'))`, since the generic transport never special-cases an event
  name); #5 (a multi-line `data:` field — both lines joined with `\n` into one `SseFrame.data`). Mock the
  underlying `dio` stream response the same way `api_client_test.dart`'s existing `call()` tests already mock
  `Dio`. Depends on T002.
```

Then update the RNF09 row of `plan.md`'s Constitution Check to cite this task number instead of only the contract document, so the "gate carried into tasks" claim is traceable to an actual task.

## Remediation for I1 (HIGH — stale turn leaks across conversation switch)

**Contract edit**, `contracts/chat-bloc.md`:

```diff
 Future<void> _onConversationSelected(ConversationSelected event, Emitter<ChatState> emit) async {
+  _turnGeneration++;   // invalidate any in-flight turn from the conversation being left (spec.md Edge Cases)
   final isOnline = await _connectivityChecker.hasConnection();
   await _loadSession(event.sessionId, emit, isOffline: !isOnline);
 }

 Future<void> _onNewConversationRequested(NewConversationRequested event, Emitter<ChatState> emit) async {
+  _turnGeneration++;   // same rationale as above
   final current = state;
   final isOffline = current is ChatReady ? current.isOffline : false;
   await _chatRepository.setLastActiveSessionId(null);
   emit(ChatReady(sessionId: null, messages: const [], isOffline: isOffline, awaitingResponse: false));
 }
```

Add a 13th row to the same contract's test-scenario table:

```markdown
| 13 | `ConversationSelected`/`NewConversationRequested` dispatched while a turn is mid-stream for the conversation being left | the in-flight turn's later `TokenReceived`/`StreamDone`/`Left` items are ignored (generation mismatch) — the newly-loaded conversation's state is never mutated by the abandoned turn |
```

**Task edit**, `tasks.md` T032 (chat_bloc.dart retry handler) already touches this file last in Foundational+US1+US3; add a line to its existing scope note (or T015, whichever lands the actual `_turnGeneration++` call in `_onConversationSelected`/`_onNewConversationRequested`) referencing contract scenario #13, and add it to T034's test task:

```diff
 - [ ] T034 [P] [US3] `bloc_test` cases in `test/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_bloc_test.dart` — contract
   scenarios #9 (...) and #10 (...)
+  and #13 (switching conversations mid-stream via `ConversationSelected`/`NewConversationRequested` stops the
+  abandoned turn's later stream items from mutating the newly-loaded conversation's state).
   Depends on T032.
```

Want me to apply these edits directly to `tasks.md` and `contracts/chat-bloc.md` now?

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: no dependencies — can start immediately. **BLOCKS** every user story phase (every
  story needs `ChatBloc`'s "load a conversation" machinery at minimum).
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: depends on Foundational only. MVP.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: depends on Foundational **and** US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022) — its failure-handling
  branch is built as part of that same function and cannot be split; this phase is otherwise test-only.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational and US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022), which it reuses verbatim
  for the retry's own stream consumption.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: depends on Foundational only — independent of US1/US2/US3's own tasks (no shared
  code with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery).
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7)**: depends on Foundational's `_loadSession`/`ChatSessionsBloc` cache-fallback logic
  (already built there) and on `ChatComposer` (T023, US1) for its own offline-disabling test.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each Phase

- Tasks touching the *same* file (`chat_bloc.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`,
  `service_locator.dart`, `app_router.dart`) are listed in the sequential order they must be applied.
- Tasks creating a *new* file with no dependency on that phase's other new files are marked `[P]`.
- Test tasks are marked `[P]` relative to each other (distinct test files); each still depends on its
  corresponding implementation task(s) existing to pass.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T001, T004–T009, T014, T015, T017 (Foundational's entities/events/states/widgets/transport) can all run in
  parallel — ten independent files with no cross-dependencies among them.
- T011 and T012 (local cache, remote data source) can run in parallel with each other once T001–T009 land.
- All test tasks within a single user story phase can run in parallel with each other.
- User Story 4 (side menu) can be implemented in parallel with User Stories 1–3 (the live conversation) by a
  second developer, since neither `ChatSessionsBloc` nor `AppDrawer`'s "CONVERSAS" section shares any code path
  with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery.
